title: Powered-On VM with VMware Tools Not Running
exclusions: Returns the latest complete VM inventory record when `summary.runtime.powerState=poweredOn` and documented `guest.toolsRunningStatus` is not `guestToolsRunning`. Broadcom defines `guestToolsNotRunning` as Tools not running and `guestToolsExecutingScripts` as starting; this rule reports the exact non-running state rather than calling it absent, outdated, unsupported, unhealthy or noncompliant. Splunk inventory documents `guest.toolsRunningStatus`, `guest.toolsVersion`, and `config.tools.toolsVersion`, but not the newer version-status property as a default indexed field, so this rule makes no Tools currency claim. It does not cover powered-off VMs, templates, open-vm-tools package policy, guest-agent feature health, heartbeat, driver state, auto-upgrade eligibility, vulnerability, or current state beyond inventory freshness. It installs, starts and upgrades nothing.
evidence: After deployment, retain VM/guest/owner inventory; vCenter/add-on and Tools/open-vm-tools support matrix; representative `VMInv:VirtualMachine` records with VM identity, power state, guest.toolsRunningStatus, guest/config Tools versions, guest OS, host, vCenter and event/index times; inventory/DCN/field/freshness health; current vSphere Client comparison; approved maintenance/exceptions; version-controlled `powered_on_vm_tools_not_running` search, ACL, schedule, dispatches and rows; runbook/dashboard and disposition; and dated running, not-running, starting, powered-off, template, blank-state, stale, replay and delayed tests. This source review created no Tools state change, inventory event, search execution, upgrade, alert, incident or production validation evidence.

controlTest.positiveScenario: In isolated VM inventory fixtures, create two powered-on non-template VMs with distinct UUIDs and `guest.toolsRunningStatus` values `guestToolsNotRunning` and `guestToolsExecutingScripts`; provide guest/config Tools versions and fresh timestamps. Expect exactly two rows preserving each exact state and UC-2.1.18.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Expect zero rows for `guestToolsRunning`, powered-off or suspended VMs, templates, wrong source/index/sourcetype, blank VM identity/power/tools state, stale records outside the closed range, and exact replay. Separate health must expose missing inventory, unknown/new enum values, blank Tools fields, delayed collection and disagreement with current vSphere state.

dataSources: Primary source is vCenter VM inventory collected through Splunk Add-on for VMware Metrics with pool task `vminv` into the deployment-selected inventory index (documented default `index=vmware-inv`), `source=VMInv:VirtualMachine`, and `sourcetype=vmware_inframon:inv:vm`. Required documented fields are VM `uuid`/`name`, `summary.runtime.powerState`, `config.template`, `guest.toolsRunningStatus`, `guest.toolsVersion`, `config.tools.toolsVersion`, guest OS, runtime host/vCenter and collection/index time. Current vSphere Client/API state, guest package/service telemetry, support policy, maintenance and owner data corroborate.
app: Splunk Add-on for VMware Metrics (Splunkbase 5089) collects VM inventory through vCenter and DCNs. A local VM-operations app owns source freshness, enum drift, owner/maintenance enrichment, saved search, tests, dashboard, routing and runbook.
spl:
index=vmware-inv source="VMInv:VirtualMachine" sourcetype="vmware_inframon:inv:vm" earliest=-2h@h latest=-1h@h
| eval vm_name=coalesce(nullif(trim(name),""),nullif(trim('summary.config.name'),"")), vm_uuid=coalesce(nullif(trim(uuid),""),nullif(trim('config.uuid'),"")), power_state=trim('summary.runtime.powerState'), tools_running_status=trim('guest.toolsRunningStatus'), guest_tools_version=trim('guest.toolsVersion'), configured_tools_version=trim('config.tools.toolsVersion'), is_template=lower(trim(tostring('config.template'))), vcenter=lower(coalesce(nullif(trim(vcenter),""),nullif(trim(host),"")))
| where len(vm_name)>0 AND len(vm_uuid)>0 AND len(vcenter)>0 AND power_state="poweredOn" AND is_template!="true" AND len(tools_running_status)>0
| stats latest(_time) AS inventory_time latest(_indextime) AS inventory_index_time latest(tools_running_status) AS tools_running_status latest(guest_tools_version) AS guest_tools_version latest(configured_tools_version) AS configured_tools_version latest('guest.guestFullName') AS guest_os latest('summary.runtime.host') AS esxi_host BY vcenter vm_uuid vm_name
| where tools_running_status!="guestToolsRunning"
| eval finding="powered_on_vm_tools_not_running", use_case="UC-2.1.18"
| table inventory_time vcenter vm_uuid vm_name esxi_host guest_os tools_running_status guest_tools_version configured_tools_version finding inventory_index_time use_case
| sort 0 vcenter vm_name
description: Reports each latest powered-on, non-template VM inventory record whose VMware Tools running-status enum is anything other than `guestToolsRunning`. Each row preserves the exact status and reported versions without claiming that Tools is missing or outdated.
value: Tools services support guest visibility and coordinated virtualization operations, so an unexpected non-running state can complicate maintenance and incident response. Precise status reporting lets VM and workload owners distinguish a stopped service, startup transition, unsupported guest or stale inventory before attempting repair.
implementation: Collect and prove the documented VM inventory fields, schedule the delayed hourly latest-state search, and operate separate inventory freshness/enum health. Reconcile findings with current vSphere and guest service/package state, maintenance and support policy; route to owners and never auto-start or upgrade Tools from inventory alone.
visualization: Use a VM table with inventory time, vCenter, UUID/name, host, guest OS, exact Tools running state, reported guest/config versions, power/template state, freshness, owner, maintenance and disposition. Add status/guest-OS trends plus separate stale/missing/unknown-enum panels. Do not label rows `outdated` or `noncompliant` without a separately sourced version policy.
schema: vCenter VirtualMachine inventory with native VMware Tools running-status enum
dataModelAcceleration: No CIM dataset documents vSphere VM power/template state with guest Tools status/version. Raw latest inventory and explicit freshness remain authoritative.

knownFalsePositives:
A non-running inventory state can be expected or transient.

1. **Guest boot or shutdown transition** — Tools may be starting while inventory says powered on. Check guest uptime, subsequent fresh inventory and startup timeout.

2. **Approved maintenance** — package/service work can stop Tools temporarily. Match exact VM, change and finite window; verify restoration.

3. **Unsupported or intentionally agentless guest** — appliance/vendor policy may prohibit or omit Tools. Confirm current support documentation, owner and reviewed exception.

4. **Open VM Tools service variation** — Linux distributions package and manage open-vm-tools differently. Verify guest package/service and support state rather than assuming proprietary Tools absence.

5. **Stale incremental inventory** — DCN backlog, vCenter/API error or unchanged-field behavior can leave an old status. Compare current vSphere Client/API and inventory health.

6. **VM restore, clone or migration** — identity and guest state can transition after recovery or movement. Correlate lifecycle events and use UUID.

7. **Guest hang or network isolation** — Tools not running may be a symptom of a broader guest failure. Check VM console/heartbeat/application evidence before service-only remediation.

8. **Unknown enum/schema drift** — newer APIs or extraction changes can produce unexpected values. Route to telemetry health; do not silently classify as not running.

**Suppression mechanism:** use a governed post-result lookup keyed by vCenter and VM UUID, exact expected state/reason, owner, support evidence, start and finite expiry. Retain unsuppressed inventory and stale/unknown-state health; never suppress by guest OS alone.

detailedImplementation:
## Prerequisites and supported claim

Assign vSphere, guest OS, application and Splunk owners. Inventory VM UUID, name, vCenter/host, guest family, power/template state, Tools implementation, owner, maintenance and support exception. Broadcom defines three running-status values: `guestToolsRunning`, `guestToolsNotRunning` and `guestToolsExecutingScripts`. This rule reports non-running state only. Version compliance requires a separate, authoritative version policy and version-status source.

## Step 1 — Collect and prove VM inventory

Deploy supported Splunk Add-on for VMware Metrics with read-only vCenter API access over TCP 443 and `vminv` in the collection pool. Verify actual output at documented default `index=vmware-inv`, `source=VMInv:VirtualMachine`, `sourcetype=vmware_inframon:inv:vm` or change only the local index.

Compare representative records with vSphere Client VM > Summary. Prove UUID/name, `summary.runtime.powerState`, `config.template`, `guest.toolsRunningStatus`, `guest.toolsVersion`, `config.tools.toolsVersion`, guest OS, runtime host, vCenter, `_time` and `_indextime`. Splunk's Inventory Reference documents running status and versions; do not assume `toolsVersionStatus2` is indexed unless a separately supported and tested collection contract adds it.

Build independent health for expected VMs, last vminv success/records_written, inventory age, blank fields, unknown enum, duplicate UUID, rename/host move, vCenter authentication, DCN backlog and current-state disagreement.

## Step 2 — Save the latest-state search

Save sidecar SPL as `powered_on_vm_tools_not_running`, hourly. Its range is one complete hour delayed by one hour. Adjust after measuring inventory cadence and p99 delay, preserving a closed range.

The search normalizes documented aliases, requires powered-on non-template VM identity and status, then takes the time-latest status/version fields per vCenter/UUID/name. Only exact `guestToolsRunning` is excluded. `guestToolsExecutingScripts` remains visible because prolonged startup deserves review. No version comparison or `toolsOk` legacy field is used.

## Step 3 — Validate inventory and guest reality

Test each enum, powered-off/suspended, template, blank state, unknown state, stale and duplicate record, same name/different UUID, rename, migration, delayed/future time and wrong source. Confirm a non-running row does not say not installed/outdated.

In isolated supported guests, use approved service stop/start and boot tests for proprietary Tools and open-vm-tools. Compare vSphere Client, API, Splunk inventory, guest service manager and package version. Measure inventory propagation and startup duration. Do not stop Tools on production to create a heartbeat.

## Step 4 — Operationalize and respond

Dashboard exact status, inventory freshness, guest/version context, owner and maintenance. Triage by verifying raw current inventory; confirming VM power/template and recent lifecycle events; checking vSphere Client; inspecting guest reachability, service/package logs and support policy; then classifying startup, maintenance, unsupported guest, stale data, service failure or broader guest outage.

Do not automatically mount installers, upgrade Tools, start services, reboot guests, modify upgrade policy or power cycle a VM. Guest changes require workload approval, backups/snapshots policy, compatibility, maintenance and rollback. Close with fresh running state or a finite approved exception and healthy inventory.

## Step 5 — Troubleshoot

- No inventory: verify `vminv`, API credentials/443, scheduler/DCN, forwarding, index/RBAC and expected VM coverage.
- Status blank: inspect raw inventory, guest support and Tools presence; route extraction/collection failures separately.
- Status remains starting: compare guest service logs, boot state, scripts and fresh API data.
- vSphere says running but Splunk does not: align inventory time, collection cadence, UUID/vCenter and incremental update health.
- Version fields differ: guest and config version properties have distinct contexts; preserve both and do not infer compliance.
- Many findings after upgrade: inspect schema/enum, add-on/DCN backlog and guest compatibility before bulk remediation.

Keep draft status until VMware, guest and Splunk owners validate fields, freshness, fixtures and safe response. Documentation review is not production health validation.
grandmaExplanation: We find powered-on virtual machines whose helper service is not reported as running. The team checks whether the machine is still starting, under maintenance, unsupported, or actually having a problem before trying to repair it.
hardware: vCenter-managed VMware virtual machines. Guest OS, VMware Tools/open-vm-tools package, service model and support policy determine expected status.
